thread:
marie-cs: Drafting a customer-facing notice for Dedicated/Private customers in us-west-2. We observed repeated ECC/Xid errors on a small number of GPUs and are rotating the affected node. Draft below — please review technical accuracy and customer impact. @sam-eng-sre @lee-platform @tasha-ops

auto-monitor-bot: ALERT: GPU_HEALTH_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED host=gpu-uw2-14 errors=5 last_xid=31

sam-eng-sre: Quick recap: multiple correctable ECC events escalated into Xid=31 (internal GPU fault) on GPU slot 2 of node gpu-uw2-14. We're draining the node, migrating active workloads to reserve pools, and scheduling a physical card replacement. ETA for replacement + warmup ~ 4-6h (vendor ETA updated later).

sam-eng-sre: Logs:```
[2026-02-28T03:14:12Z] nvidia: Xid (31): Internal Error, GPU-0
[2026-02-28T03:18:01Z] kernel: GPU ECC corrected errors: 12 -> escalated
[2026-02-28T03:22:03Z] platform: drain triggered for node gpu-uw2-14
```

lee-platform: Tone suggestions: emphasize no data exfiltration, brief interruption window, and available fallbacks (auto-failover to shared capacity or migration to other dedicated pools). Also add billing protection/credit promise for impacted time window.

marie-cs: Draft notice for review (will send via support channel + direct email to Dedicated/Private contacts):

"Hello <CustomerName>,

We're emailing to let you know we detected hardware degradation on a GPU node in the us-west-2 Dedicated/Private pool serving your workload. At 03:14 UTC our monitoring flagged ECC/Xid errors; to protect your workloads we drained the affected node and initiated automatic failover to alternate capacity.

What this means for you:
- Active requests may reconnect briefly (seconds → a few minutes) as traffic is routed to replacement hosts.
- We do not expect data loss or access outside your environment.
- Networking: VPC/private networking is preserved; there may be short session rebinds but no public IP exposure.
- Billing: we will not charge for tokens processed during the drain window and will issue credits for any sustained throughput degradation.

Replacement timeline: we’ve engaged our hardware partner and expect a full card replacement and node validation within ~4–6 hours. We’ll notify you once the node returns to service.

If you notice anything unexpected, please reply to this thread or contact support@redwood.com.

Thanks,
Marie — Customer Success"

marie-cs: cc: internal links added (ops playbook + ticket): https://internal.redwood/playbooks/gpu-node-rotation and ticket HW-8421

tasha-ops: Add ops contact: @oncall-ops. Also call out that we prefetched model weights and warmed KV caches on receivers to reduce cold-start impact.

jordan-customer: Thanks for the transparency. For Private deployments can you confirm whether IPs will change or if there will be any VPC peering impact?

lee-platform: For Private/VPC customers: we retain ENI attachment where possible; if customers use floating IPs there may be short rebinds. No peering changes. Adding one sentence to the notice.

sam-eng-sre: Technical approve — added that we ran cache warmup and that logs are retained for 30 days. Also note: we've limited scheduling to healthy hosts; flag/trace for postmortem: tag=HW-8421.

marie-cs: Final copy ready to send at 10:05 UTC. Will post to affected customers and the Dedicated status page. :white_check_mark:

auto-monitor-bot: UPDATE: node gpu-uw2-14 state=drained; workloads migrated to ded-reserve-1; vendor ETA updated to 4h for replacement.

jordan-customer: Appreciate the quick handling, please keep us posted.

marie-cs: Will follow up with a final confirmation when node is back in service.
